summary: The dominant 0x55a500-0x575e30 'units' mega-block (biped.c/unit.c/unit_animation.c/vehicle.c) is well supported by seeds, callee cohesion, and marker strings ('stand','unarmed','left hand'), and its internal sub-boundaries hold up under spot decompilation (pack.py checks on 0x561140, 0x5756f0, 0x55b440, 0x577e40 all confirm unit/object-datum access patterns or network message dispatch consistent with the assigned module). The 0x575fa0-0x577e40 GameSpy/bungie.net networking block and the version-string pair at 0x578190/0x5781c0 also check out on decompilation (embedded '01.01.260.1'-style version string plus a version-compare routine, tied to the adjacent update-check code). The one clear problem is the tail run 0x5782b0-0x57af10, labelled lib:other.

disputes.reason: Decompiling this run (0x5782b0-0x57af10, ~30 functions) shows it is a hand-written C++/STL requirements-language interpreter, not a recognized third-party library. FUN_00578ff0 (pack.py) explicitly loads and string-compares every single D3DCAPS9 field name ("Caps2","RasterCaps","MaxTextureWidth","VertexShaderVersion","MaxSimultaneousTextures", etc.) plus calls GetVersionExA and compares OS strings ("win95"..

), and gamespy_get_client_key_hash@0x579690 (a bogus Ghidra name - its body is actually the '==','!=','>=','<=' comparison-operator tokenizer for the same grammar, not any real GameSpy SDK function) feeds directly into the same parser (FUN_00578b20/578ef0/578f80/578fa0). Strings like 'OverallGraphicDetail'/'MaxOverallGraphicDetail'/'Requirements'/'applytoall'/'audiovendor' point to a Halo-PC-specific hardware-compatibility/graphics-quality-autodetect feature that Gearbox added for the PC port - i.e. genuine engine/port code, not D3DX9, CRT, GameSpy, Bink, or Vorbis (the only things the task's fencing rules call out for lib:*). Some entries in the run also have nonzero external caller counts (0x5782b0 callers=6, 0x57af10 callers=6, 0x5785b0 callers=9), contradicting the evidence's 'no Blam callers' claim. Recommend re-labelling this run 'unknown' (safest, since shell vs rasterizer can't be distinguished from the current evidence) rather than lib:other; the assignor's own notes already flagged this same doubt ('shell or rasterizer are the plausible alternatives') but still emitted a lib:* label. Same reasoning applies to every function in the run (0x578310, 0x578390, 0x5783b0, 0x5783c0, 0x5783e0, 0x5783f0, 0x578410, 0x5785b0, 0x578630, 0x5786a0, 0x5788f0, 0x5789d0, 0x578a00, 0x578a20, 0x578ad0, 0x578b20, 0x578c60, 0x578cf0, 0x578ef0, 0x578f80, 0x578fa0, 0x578ff0, 0x579690, 0x579ef0, 0x579fe0, 0x57a010, 0x57a220, 0x57a320, 0x57a3e0, 0x57a680, 0x57aa40, 0x57ae50, 0x57af10), and per the boundary notes the same block continues into slice 13 (0x57b470 onward), so that continuation should get the same corrected label.
